about: Domaine Olga Raffault lies in Savigny-en-Véron, west of the town of Chinon, close to the Vienne river. In 1931 Olga married Pierre Raffault, a fellow grower from Savigny, and together they held three hectares of vines, though asparagus was their main crop at first. After Pierre died in 1947, Olga kept the estate going. Today her granddaughter Sylvie Raffault, Sylvie’s husband Éric de la Vigerie and their son Arnaud farm about 25 hectares, certified organic, along the Vienne.

Chinon is known for Cabernet Franc, but a little white Chinon is made from Chenin Blanc. Chenin des Picasses comes from young vines the family planted at the top of the slope in Les Picasses, their best-known vineyard, where clay sits over chalky limestone. The cuvée was first made in 2020. In that debut vintage it was fermented and aged in 500-litre demi-muids two and three years old, without malolactic fermentation, to keep its natural acidity.

Expect lemon, quince and apple with a chalky, mineral edge, a note of beeswax or bee pollen and a faint touch of vanilla from the older casks. Chenin of this kind has firm acidity and tends to gain depth as the vines age; a critic tasting the first vintage expected the wine’s middle to fill out as these young vines mature over the next decade.
facts: Top of Les Picasses slope; young vines
Older 500 L demi-muids, no malolactic (as in the first vintage, 2020)
